name: Question 17
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081209/assets/7ecbb53bb87156d11f9a9d8021182cdfb8c0c1749cd028780377bb61f32adf43.png)

The graph of the function $f(x)$, which is defined on $[-3,6]$, is shown above. It consists of the arc of the semi-circle centered at $(0,0)$ with radius $3,$ and two line segments. Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[-3,5].$
worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,3].$ The corresponding region is a semi-cirle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5-(-3)}\cdot (\frac{9\pi }{2}+2) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{16}+\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17

The graph of the function f(x), which is defined on [−3,6], is shown above. It consists of the arc of the semi-circle centered at (0,0) with radius 3, and two line segments. Find the average value of f(x) on [−3,5].

a
9π16+14
b
9π8−14
c
9π2+12
d
9π8+18
e
9π16+12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The average value of a function on a given interval [a,b] is favg=1b−a∫abf(x)dx.

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write ∫−35f(x)dx=∫−33f(x)dx⏟A1+∫35f(x)dx⏟A2.

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−3,3]. The corresponding region is a semi-cirle, so we find the area using the formula:

A1=12πr2=12π⋅32=9π2.

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[3,5]. The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

A2=12bh=12⋅2⋅2=2.

So, we obtain

∫−35f(x)dx=A1+A2=9π2+2.

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get favg=1b−a∫abf(x)dx=15−(−3)⋅(9π2+2)=9π16+14.
